_comment: Declared derivation: text.txt == extract -> slice -> drop_lines -> pre -> reflow -> mechanical -> corrections, byte-exact against text_sha256. Verified by scripts/derive_text.py.

slice.end_contains: procedures for the peaceful settlement of disputes.
slice._reason: Section C of Part two of the shared compendium ST/SPACE/61/Rev.3 (English), lines 1941-2121 of 5,175. The end anchor is short enough to sit inside one raw line: 'end_contains' matches the RAW extraction, so a longer phrase spans a line break and never fires, which silently runs the slice on into the next instrument.

drop_lines._reason: Running page numbers, alone on a line.

Footnote lines, whose marker digits are glued to a capital ('10Official Records of the General Assembly...'). NOTE: this removes only the FIRST line of a footnote. The stored text retains the orphaned continuation 'and Corr.1).' as its own paragraph, so this recipe reproduces that faithfully rather than tidying it away — the stored bytes are what must be reproduced, defects included.

_pre_reason: This instrument uses three enumeration conventions the volume runs together but the stored text separates: a bare 'Principle I' heading on its own line, lettered definitions '(a)'-'(e)', and numbered paragraphs. split_principle_headings is safe here precisely because the headings carry no text on the same line — resolution 47/68 writes 'Principle 1. Applicability of international law' with substantive text following on the same line and must NOT use this rule.
_reflow_reason: Undo column wrapping; 'tight' collapses the blank runs left where page furniture was removed.
_mechanical_reason: -layout pads with space runs to reproduce the printed column.

corrections.to: Principles Relating to Remote Sensing of the Earth from Outer Space
corrections._reason: Removes the compendium's section label 'C.' and the trailing footnote reference marker '9'. Both belong to the volume's apparatus, not to the resolution's title.

_verified.note: Third record cut from the shared English compendium. FOUR of the five corrections are NO-BREAK SPACE differences (U+00A0 where the extraction yields U+0020) that no reader would ever see. They cluster at points where the PDF broke a word or a date across a line, so they are artefacts of how the stored text was assembled rather than typographic choices. Enumerated exhaustively — the stored text contains exactly four U+00A0 characters and each is accounted for here — because a byte-equality claim is worth nothing if the remaining bytes are unexplained.
